A.depoimento: I have ordered the construction of an archer and dispatched my forces to take the neutral villages of Santarem and Evora. With my archers leading the charge, I expect swift victories, and I will expand my kingdom's borders!
A.plano: Capture Santarem and Evora to secure a foothold. Next turn, build archers and spearmen in all three villages, then send armies from Santarem to Coimbra and Badajoz, and from Evora to Faro. Continue expanding along the roads, capturing neutral villages and eventually confronting the enemy. Aim to reach 18 villages quickly while building a strong army.

B.depoimento: My armies struck at both neutral villages simultaneously. The spearmen lead the assault on Tarragona, while archers and knights overwhelm Girona. At Barcelona, I train an archer to rebuild my ranks.
B.plano: I have attacked Tarragona and Girona with split forces. Tarragona: 5 spearmen, 1 archer, 1 knight. Girona: 3 archers, 2 knights. I built an archer at Barcelona. Next turn, I will survey the newly captured villages (Zaragoza, Castellon from Tarragona; Huesca from Girona) and plan further expansion. Tarragona will have a garrison of 4; Girona 2. I must reinforce them and explore the road network.

B.depoimento: Orders are given for a major expansion! My forces from Tarragona will strike Castellon and Zaragoza, while Girona's army takes Huesca. Barcelona is on war production, building a spearman and an archer, and sending its archer to Tarragona. We are moving to secure the northern route!
B.plano: I am launching a triple attack this turn to expand my territory. Tarragona will attack Castellon and Zaragoza, while Girona attacks Huesca. Barcelona will build a spearman and an archer, and send its existing archer to reinforce Tarragona. I must remember to consolidate my newly conquered villages and start building up their economies.

B.depoimento: King B orders a full assault on Pamplona, sending every available soldier from Huesca. Reinforcements march to Castellon and Girona to secure the borders. The army grows as new troops are trained in the capital and Tarragona.
B.plano: Attacking Pamplona with all troops from Huesca to expand territory. Reinforcing Castellon from Tarragona for the upcoming attack on Valencia. Building troops in Barcelona, Tarragona, and Girona to grow the army and defend Girona. Next turn: consolidate Pamplona, launch attack on Valencia, and begin building in newly conquered villages. Consider reinforcing Huesca from Zaragoza next turn to avoid leaving it empty.

A.depoimento: We have launched a coordinated assault on the neutral territories, sending our elite archers and spearmen to capture Badajoz and Faro. Simultaneously, our knights from the capital are marching to reinforce Santarem, ensuring our lines remain strong and ready for the next push. The expansion begins now!
A.plano: Our immediate goal is to secure our borders by capturing the nearby neutral villages of Badajoz and Faro, which will provide us with vital resources and a stepping stone for further expansion. We will reinforce Santarem from Lisboa to prepare for the next wave of attacks on Coimbra and deeper into the peninsula. In the long term, we will push north and east to connect our territories and eventually confront the enemy capital in Barcelona, aiming to hold 18 villages to secure victory.

B.depoimento: We launch our attack on Valencia from Castellon, sending all available troops. To secure the next objective, Madrid, we are concentrating forces in Zaragoza by sending reinforcements from Pamplona and Tarragona. Barcelona sends troops to Tarragona to keep it strong. We are building across our empire to grow our army.
B.plano: Attack Valencia from Castellon to expand territory. Send all troops from Pamplona and Tarragona to Zaragoza to prepare for the attack on Madrid next turn. Send troops from Barcelona to Tarragona to maintain its garrison. Build troops in all available villages to grow the army.

A.depoimento: Turn 5: We have consolidated our recent conquests of Badajoz and Faro. I am sending the elite knights from Santarem to capture Coimbra, the gateway to the north. The rest of the army is marching to reinforce our capital and the newly captured territories. We are building archers and spearmen to swell our ranks for the push into the unexplored lands. The campaign for the peninsula is underway!
A.plano: Consolidate forces towards the northern hub. Capture Coimbra this turn with the Santarem garrison, then reinforce it with troops from Lisboa next turn. Move all troops from the southern villages (Badajoz, Faro, Evora) to the main hubs (Lisboa, Santarem) to prepare for the next wave of expansions towards Porto and Salamanca. Build archers and spearmen in the resource-producing villages to grow the army.

B.depoimento: King B's armies move on Madrid! Four archers from Zaragoza storm the neutral city, seeking to expand our dominion and uncover the enemy's secrets. Reinforcements from Tarragona, Girona, Huesca, and Barcelona march to Zaragoza to keep our war machine strong. Our builders work day and night, forging archers, spearmen, and knights to swell our ranks. The kingdom grows!
B.plano: Attack Madrid with Zaragoza's 4 archers to secure a neutral village and gain western intel. Reinforce Zaragoza with troops from Tarragona, Girona, Huesca, and Barcelona to rebuild its army. Build archers and spearmen across all available villages to prepare for attacks on Teruel, Murcia, and Burgos next turn. Next turn, explore west from Madrid and decide whether to take Teruel or push into enemy territory.

A.depoimento: Turn 6. I have consolidated my forces towards the northern hub. Troops from Lisboa, Santarem, and Evora are marching to reinforce Coimbra, the recently captured village. I have ordered the construction of infantry and archers across my producing villages to grow my army for the upcoming assaults on Porto and Salamanca.
A.plano: Consolidate the northern front. Move all available troops from Lisboa, Santarem, and Evora to Coimbra to create a massive strike force. Next turn, launch coordinated attacks on Porto (using spearmen to counter knights) and Salamanca (using archers to counter spearmen). Secure the northern route, then push towards Madrid and the enemy capital Barcelona. Keep the southern villages producing troops to feed the main army.

A.depoimento: Ordered the assembly of a strike force at Coimbra and launched a two-pronged attack: spearmen and knights against Porto (leveraging the spearman-knight counter) and archers against Salamanca (leveraging the archer-spearmen counter). Reinforcements from Lisboa, Santarem, and Badajoz are marching to Coimbra to sustain the push. All six villages are producing troops for the campaign.
A.plano: Launch coordinated attacks on Porto and Salamanca from Coimbra this turn: spearmen+knight vs Porto (counter bonus), archers vs Salamanca (counter bonus). After capturing both, push to Vigo and Madrid. Keep reinforcing Coimbra from Lisboa, Santarem, and Badajoz. Build troops at all villages to feed the northern advance. Southern villages (Badajoz, Faro) build archers for future push towards Toledo and Sevilha.

A.depoimento: This turn we strengthen our borders. Knights overwhelm Vigo, and archers and knights pour into Salamanca. Our villages produce troops for the next offensives.
A.plano: Reinforce Salamanca with knights and archers while our knights take Vigo. Build troops everywhere and send reinforcements to the south. Next turn, attack Madrid from Salamanca and Toledo from Badajoz.

B.depoimento: King B's armies advance! Archers from Zaragoza march to seize Teruel, while reinforcements strengthen Madrid and Pamplona. Our forges burn day and night, crafting spears and armor for the battles to come. The path to victory is paved with iron and wood.
B.plano: This turn we focus on capturing Teruel with 4 archers from Zaragoza. We also send 2 archers to Madrid and 4 spearman to Pamplona to reinforce and prepare for future attacks. We build troops in Zaragoza, Valencia, Madrid, Tarragona, and Pamplona to replenish our forces. Next turn we will attack Burgos from Pamplona with 7 spearman, and we will consider attacking Murcia or Salamanca. Must not forget to move the spearman from Pamplona to Burgos once they are ready.

A.depoimento: King A orders the assault on Madrid with the full garrison of Salamanca. Reinforcements from Coimbra are sent to secure Salamanca, while troops from Santarem, Faro, and Porto gather at Badajoz and Vigo to prepare for the conquest of Toledo, Sevilha, and Burgos. Builds are ordered across all villages to strengthen the army.
A.plano: Attack Madrid from Salamanca to secure the border and open the road east. Send reinforcements from Coimbra to Salamanca to defend it after the attack. Gather troops in Badajoz (from Santarem and Faro) and Vigo (from Porto) to conquer Toledo, Sevilha, and Burgos next turns. Build knights and archers everywhere to maintain momentum.

A.depoimento: King A launches a massive three-pronged attack this turn! Madrid's archers and knights strike Toledo, Badajoz's forces assault Sevilha, and Vigo's spearmen and knights ride to conquer Burgos. With the counter triangle bonuses on our side, we expect swift victories to secure three new villages and bring us closer to our goal of 18 villages!
A.plano: Conquer Toledo, Sevilha, and Burgos this turn to expand our territory to 13 villages. Use Madrid's archers and knight to attack Toledo (counter bonus), Badajoz's mixed force to attack Sevilha, and Vigo's spearmen and knights to attack Burgos (counter bonus). After conquering these, consolidate our hold by building up troops in the new villages and preparing to push east towards Zaragoza and the enemy capital.

A.depoimento: Our army from Badajoz is about to conquer Sevilha, securing our western flank. This turn, we send reinforcements to Badajoz from Santarem and Faro, which will march to Sevilha next turn once it is conquered. We launch an attack on Teruel with Toledo's archers and knight, aiming to push towards Valencia and expand our territory. We reinforce Madrid and Burgos with spearman to hold the line against Zaragoza and Pamplona. Our Coimbra forces move to Salamanca, ready to deploy where needed. We also build knights across our realm to strengthen our army for the next push east.
A.plano: Our army from Badajoz is about to conquer Sevilha, securing our western flank. This turn, we send reinforcements to Badajoz from Santarem and Faro, which will march to Sevilha next turn once it is conquered. We launch an attack on Teruel with Toledo's archers and knight, aiming to push towards Valencia and expand our territory. We reinforce Madrid and Burgos with spearman to hold the line against Zaragoza and Pamplona. Our Coimbra forces move to Salamanca, ready to deploy where needed. We also build knights across our realm to strengthen our army for the next push east.

B.depoimento: On Turn 12, King B orders all villages to convert their resources into knights, unleashing a swift and powerful cavalry force. We launch simultaneous offensives on four fronts: Valencia strikes Teruel, Zaragoza assaults Madrid, Pamplona attacks Burgos, and Castellon marches on Murcia. Reinforcements are dispatched from Barcelona to Tarragona, and from Girona and Huesca to Zaragoza to secure our borders and prepare for the push into the unexplored south. The tide of the war is turning in our favor!
B.plano: Launch a massive four-front offensive to conquer Teruel, Madrid, Burgos, and Murcia, bringing our held villages to 12. Convert all resources to knights for speed and power. Reinforce Tarragona and Zaragoza to prepare for the next turn's push into the unexplored south.

A.depoimento: I have launched a two-pronged attack, sending the Salamanca army to Madrid and the Teruel garrison to Valencia. Meanwhile, I am reinforcing my southern borders, moving troops from Badajoz to Toledo and from Evora to Sevilha, while building new troops across the kingdom to prepare for the next phase of the campaign.
A.plano: Attack Madrid from Salamanca and Valencia from Teruel this turn. Reinforce Toledo from Badajoz and Teruel from Toledo to prepare for the next attacks on Cordoba and Zaragoza. Move Evora's troops to Sevilha to gather strength for Cordoba. Build troops across all villages to maximize production.

B.depoimento: King B's war council is clear. The seven knights of Castellon ride hard for Teruel, aiming to break the enemy's western border. Valencia forges two new knights to stand guard against sudden raids. Zaragoza sends two steel-clad brothers south to strengthen Madrid's walls. In every province, the forges burn bright, hammering out the knights that will carry King B's banner to victory.
B.plano: Attacking Teruel with 7 knights from Castellon to expand territory and reduce enemy presence. Built 2 knights in Valencia to raise its defense from 5 to 10, protecting it from enemy counterattack. Sent 2 knights from Zaragoza to reinforce Madrid against potential assaults from Salamanca or Toledo. Building knights across the realm to grow the army for future campaigns. Next turn: assess the battle at Teruel, repair any losses, and continue pushing into enemy territory while watching for enemy movements on Valencia or Madrid.

A.depoimento: We launch a multi-front assault this turn. Toledo and Sevilha converge on Cordoba, while Madrid strikes Zaragoza and Burgos attacks Pamplona. Salamanca reinforces Madrid, and Vigo strengthens Burgos. Our forces are built up across the realm to sustain the campaign.
A.plano: Attack Cordoba from Toledo and Sevilha this turn to secure the southern route. Simultaneously attack Zaragoza from Madrid and Pamplona from Burgos to open the northern and eastern fronts. Reinforce Madrid with Salamanca's spearmen and Burgos with Vigo's troops for the next wave of expansions. Build archers and knights across all villages to maintain momentum.

B.depoimento: Turn 15: I ordered the conquest of Murcia and Burgos to expand my territory. I sent knights from Valencia to Murcia and from Pamplona to Burgos. I reinforced my border villages of Zaragoza and Teruel to prepare for the next pushes into enemy territory. I also built troops in all my villages to grow my army.
B.plano: Conquering Murcia and Burgos to expand territory and reach 11 villages. Reinforced Zaragoza and Teruel to prepare for attacks on Madrid and Toledo. Next turn: assess battles, repair losses, and plan the next pushes. Watch for enemy counterattacks on Zaragoza or Teruel.

B.depoimento: King B's forces strike on all fronts this turn! Tarragona's mighty host marches on Zaragoza, while Teruel and Burgos sweep aside the weak garrisons of Toledo and Vigo. In the south, Valencia's spearmen rush to defend Murcia, and Pamplona's archers reinforce Burgos. We aim to conquer three villages today and bring our total to thirteen, closing in on the enemy capital!
B.plano: Launch a three-pronged assault: Tarragona takes Zaragoza, Teruel takes Toledo, Burgos takes Vigo. Reinforce Murcia with Valencia's spearmen, Burgos with Pamplona's archers, and Huesca with Girona's knight. Next turn, assess losses, rebuild troops, and prepare pushes toward Madrid and Cordoba.

A.depoimento: I have launched a massive pincer movement. My northern army takes Vigo while my southern army strikes Toledo. I have emptied the interior to reinforce the borders, moving troops from Sevilha, Coimbra, Faro, Santarem, Evora, Lisboa, and Salamanca to the front lines. We now hold the initiative and will push deeper into enemy territory next turn.
A.plano: Conquer Vigo and Toledo this turn to open the northern and central fronts. Shift all troops to the border villages: reinforce Badajoz, Porto, Cordoba, and Madrid for the next wave of attacks. Next turn, attack Burgos from Vigo and Murcia from Cordoba. Build archers in all villages to maintain the flow of reinforcements.

B.depoimento: My knights storm Badajoz from Toledo while I concentrate archers at Zaragoza for the decisive blow against Madrid. The enemy's spearman-heavy garrisons demand archer-led armies, and I'm massing accordingly. Vigo is being built up for the push on Porto next turn, and I'm rebuilding losses across the realm.
B.plano: Attack Badajoz with 5 knights from Toledo (knight vs archer = x1.5 counter, 30 effective vs 15 defense, comfortable win). Build 4 archers at Zaragoza + send Pamplona's 4 archers and Huesca's 4 spearman + 2 knight there for the Madrid attack next turn. Madrid has 6 spearmen as most numerous, so I MUST have archers as my most numerous type to get the counter bonus. Build Vigo with 1 knight + 1 archer for Porto. Rebuild Toledo with 2 knights. Next turn: attack Madrid from Zaragoza with 9 archers + 4 spearman + 2 knight (archer most numerous, x1.5, ~45 effective vs 20), and Porto from Vigo with 2

A.depoimento: This turn, I launched a decisive double strike, sending the full might of Toledo to conquer the weakly defended Teruel, and Cordoba's army to crush Murcia. Simultaneously, I reinforced our border villages—sending troops from Badajoz to Toledo, Sevilha to Cordoba, Salamanca to Madrid, and Porto to Vigo—to prepare for the next wave of expansions. The enemy capital may be far, but our net is tightening as we move closer to the 18-village victory!
A.plano: Attack Teruel from Toledo and Murcia from Cordoba this turn to expand our territory to 15 villages. Next turn, launch a coordinated assault on Burgos from the reinforced Madrid and Vigo, and push east from Murcia towards Valencia. Keep building knights in Madrid, Badajoz, and Porto to counter the enemy archers, and archers in the interior to feed the fronts. We need 3 more villages to reach the 18-village threshold.

B.depoimento: I attacked Madrid with a strong archer-led army from Zaragoza. I reinforced my border villages of Zaragoza, Teruel, and Burgos to secure my positions. Ready to expand next turn.
B.plano: Attacked Madrid from Zaragoza with 8 archers, 4 spear, 3 knight (counter bonus). Reinforced Zaragoza with knights/archers from interior. Reinforced Teruel (Valencia, Castellon) and Burgos (Pamplona). Next turn: assess Madrid, build troops, prepare Toledo attack from Teruel (knights), reinforce Murcia with knights for Cordoba, consider Vigo from Burgos.

A.depoimento: I am launching a multi-pronged attack. My southern forces are taking Valencia, while my central and northern armies are gathering to strike at Madrid and Burgos. The enemy will not be able to hold the line.
A.plano: Turn 20: Attack Valencia from Murcia, reinforce Toledo from Cordoba/Badajoz, reinforce Vigo from Porto. Turn 21: Attack Madrid from Toledo, Burgos from Vigo. Turn 22: Expand north from Madrid/Burgos towards Zaragoza and Pamplona. Build archers and knights in all villages to maintain momentum.

A.depoimento: Turn 21: My armies in Toledo and Salamanca march to conquer Madrid, while Vigo's forces strike Burgos. We reinforce Valencia and Toledo to prepare for the next phase of our campaign to reach 18 villages. The enemy will not stop our expansion!
A.plano: Turn 21: Attack Madrid from Toledo and Salamanca, Burgos from Vigo. Reinforce Valencia from Murcia, Cordoba to Toledo, Sevilha to Cordoba. Turn 22: Attack Teruel from Valencia/Toledo, push towards Zaragoza from Madrid. Turn 23: Attack Castellon from Valencia, expand north. Build archers and knights in all villages to maintain momentum.

A.depoimento: This turn, I am launching a two-pronged attack. From the north, Burgos sends its full force to crush the weak garrison at Pamplona. From the east, Valencia storms Teruel. Simultaneously, I am reinforcing my border villages: Cordoba to Toledo, Porto to Salamanca, and Vigo to Burgos to hold the front lines. My industry is running at full capacity, building archers and knights everywhere to feed the war machine.
A.plano: Turn 23: Attack Pamplona from Burgos, Teruel from Valencia. Reinforce Toledo from Cordoba, Salamanca from Porto, Burgos from Vigo. Turn 24: Attack Madrid from Toledo/Salamanca/Burgos, Castellon from Valencia. Turn 25: Push towards Zaragoza from Madrid, Tarragona from Castellon. Build archers and knights in all villages to maintain momentum.

B.depoimento: Our knights strike from Zaragoza to take Teruel and Pamplona, while Huesca gets reinforcements. Our villages bustle with building as we grow our might.
B.plano: We attack Teruel and Pamplona with knights from Zaragoza to conquer them and remove threats to Castellon and Huesca. We send knights from Girona to reinforce Huesca. We build knights in all villages to rebuild our forces. We do not attack Valencia yet to keep Castellon's defense.

B.depoimento: My armies are on the move! I have ordered every available soldier to march on Zaragoza, forming a mighty host that will crush the enemy. Castellon's troops are sent to Valencia to claim it for the crown. My blacksmiths are working day and night to forge new knights and spearmen. The enemy will soon learn the cost of crossing King B!
B.plano: I am concentrating all my forces at Zaragoza to create an unassailable fortress. Castellon is attacking Valencia to conquer it and expand my territory. I am sending all troops from Teruel, Pamplona, Huesca, Tarragona, Girona, and Barcelona to Zaragoza. I am building 16 knights and 32 spearmen to rebuild my armies. I accept that I might lose Teruel and Pamplona temporarily, but I will retake them with the Zaragoza horde.

A.depoimento: Our armies have set out for Teruel and Pamplona, while reinforcements rush to shore up our vulnerable borders, especially Murcia. The builders are working overtime, churning out archers and knights. We expect to conquer two enemy villages this turn and will press the advantage next turn against Valencia. The enemy may try to counterattack, but our defenses are ready.
A.plano: We are launching a two-pronged attack this turn: Toledo strikes Teruel, Burgos strikes Pamplona, while we reinforce our borders from interior villages. We are building archers across our realm to swell our ranks, focusing on Murcia and the border cities. Next turn, we will turn our attention to Valencia, taking it from the weakened enemy. Our aim is to hold 18 villages by the end of next turn and consolidate our hold.

A.depoimento: We launched a decisive strike at Valencia, sending our full might from Murcia to crush the enemy's weak garrison and claim our 18th village. Our archers are being built in every corner of the realm to ensure our dominance.
A.plano: Take Valencia this turn with Murcia's army to reach 18 villages. Build archers across all villages to swell our ranks. Next turn, reinforce Valencia and prepare to attack Castellon and Huesca. Consolidate our hold on the new territories.

A.depoimento: Our scouts report Huesca is weakly defended. We march from Pamplona to strike them down, while reinforcing our borders from Burgos, Madrid, and Salamanca. The army grows, and the enemy's time is running out.
A.plano: Attack Huesca from Pamplona to secure our northern border and increase our village count to 19. Reinforce Pamplona from Burgos, and shift troops from Madrid and Salamanca to Toledo and Teruel to prepare for the next push into Castellon and Zaragoza. Build archers and knights across all interior villages to maintain momentum.

B.depoimento: We must strike fast and secure our borders. I am sending the Zaragoza garrison to conquer Teruel, while reinforcing Castellon and Huesca to protect against King A's forces. Our economy is strong, and we will build knights and archers to maintain the offensive.
B.plano: Attack Teruel from Zaragoza to expand territory and weaken King A. Reinforce Castellon from Tarragona and Huesca from Girona to secure borders against enemy counter-attacks. Build knights and archers in all villages to maintain military strength and leverage the counter triangle against enemy archers.
